SMTO-EXE-0046 — SMTO doesn't know what an earlier job changed

GUID: b1475ef0-7894-4e2e-a020-9f571750ae77
Slug: resource-historical-effect-unknown
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • An earlier job that worked on the same thing has finished, but SMTO can't tell everything it changed. To be safe, your new command was held back and did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the file, service or machine the earlier job was working on and note whether its change is already there. SMTO lost track of the earlier job's result, so only the real current state shows what happened.
  2. If the current state is acceptable, select Resolve forcefully by terminating job on the task's recovery card. Changes already made are kept. This clears the earlier job's hold on the resource so your waiting command can start.
  3. If that button isn't available, select Wait until the job state changes, or select Stop if you no longer need the task. SMTO only offers the forceful option when it can safely release the earlier job's hold.
  4. Only ask SMTO to redo the earlier change if step 1 showed it did not happen. Repeating a change that already happened could apply it twice.

What success looks like

  • The recovery card goes away and the task continues with your command.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, along with what you found in step 1. Don't delete SMTO's saved data or task history to get past this; it holds the record of what the earlier job did.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gateway admission rejected the new command because an earlier conflicting job has ended with historical_effect_uncertain set, so its effects on the shared resource are unknown; the new command did not run.

What this means

  • Admission found uncertain historical effects after blocking work ended and rejected the new command pending reconciliation. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Admission found uncertain historical effects after blocking work ended and rejected the new command pending reconciliation.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the prior operation's outcome and current affected resource state, keeping ended liveness separate from effect certainty.

How to fix it

  • The job was recorded as not admitted with resource_intervention_kind=historical_effect_unknown and the uncertain jobs in blocking_job_ids. Inspect the actual state of the target resource, then record a supported decision through the run's resource-reconciliation control (reset when eligible); reconciliation must not rewrite the earlier job's recorded outcome, and the earlier mutation must not be replayed without that check.
  • Inspect the current machine state and use the supported resource reconciliation decision before continuing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile the blocker before requesting another mutation. An unobservable process or uncertain effect is not proof that the earlier operation did nothing.

How to verify the fix

  • Supported reconciliation records a current valid basis for further work without rewriting the original uncertain outcome.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
